scope.design_basis: Observed patterns in FIRs and attached State FIR/MHA-order material
scope.purpose: Evidence-first criminal-network analysis ontology for FIR ingestion, extraction, normalization, candidate linking, graph construction and grounded Q&A
out_of_scope_for_v0_2: classified intelligence-only attributes not present in source
automated operational decision-making without human review
unsupported inference from absence of data

design_principles: Every derived assertion must remain traceable to source evidence.
Raw source values are immutable and must be retained alongside normalized values.
Extraction confidence and identity confidence are separate.
Document assertion, model inference and adjudicated fact are separate epistemic states.
Unknown entities are valid first-class entities.
Legal citations must not be silently converted or rewritten.
Cross-case identity links are candidates until independently resolved.
Events are first-class objects rather than implicit edges.
Provenance is part of the semantic model, not optional metadata.

rules: IDs must be stable across reprocessing when the same source entity is retained.
Raw document identifiers must never be used as the only identity key for a real-world entity.
Identity candidates use separate candidate-link identifiers until resolution.

states.meaning: The source states or asserts the claim.
Information reported by a person or secondary source inside the document.
An allegation; not an adjudicated finding.
The source identifies a subject or association as suspected.
Derived by the system from other observations.
Identity/entity resolution completed under the project's resolution rules.
The mention or entity could not be safely resolved.
Present as a claim/mention but not independently verified.
Established through a judicial/procedural source; not derivable from an FIR alone.

extraction_confidence.meaning: Confidence that text was correctly extracted and typed.

normalization_confidence.meaning: Confidence that raw value was normalized correctly.

identity_confidence.meaning: Confidence that two mentions refer to the same real-world entity.

relation_confidence.meaning: Confidence that a typed relation is supported.

event_confidence.meaning: Confidence that an event and its arguments were correctly extracted.

legal_resolution_confidence.meaning: Confidence that a raw legal citation maps to a canonical provision.

confidence_model.rule: A score must always be interpreted in the context of its field; do not create one universal confidence field.

source_location.rule: At least one precise source locator should be retained.

Document.description: Source artifact such as NIA FIR, State FIR, MHA order or annexure.

DocumentPage.description: Addressable page or page-like unit within a source document.

DocumentSegment.description: Addressable textual or visual segment inside a document/page.

MediaArtifact.description: Image, audio, video or other digital media artifact that can support observations.

Person.description: A named, described or unknown human actor.

Organization.description: A formal or informal group, institution, unit or organization mentioned in source material.

OrganizationUnit.description: Sub-unit, division, branch, battalion, committee or operational unit.

Location.description: Physical or administrative place relevant to an event, person, asset or jurisdiction.

Vehicle.description: Road vehicle or other vehicle explicitly represented in source material.

Weapon.description: Firearm or weapon represented in evidence or source narrative.

Explosive.description: Explosive substance, explosive device, detonator, fuse, cord or related material.

Narcotic.description: Controlled substance or narcotic represented in the source.

Device.description: Physical communication, computing, storage or other device.

DigitalEntity.description: Online account, handle, channel, post, video, image or platform-level digital source.

DocumentArtifact.description: Map, notebook, literature, photograph, video, digital file or other material artifact.

FinancialEntity.description: Transaction, bank account, cash holding or payment instrument.

Property.description: Residence, building, land, premises or other property relevant to a case.

Event.description: Time-bounded or temporally anchored occurrence with participants, location, objects and outcomes.

normalization_rules.rule: Preserve exact raw name; normalized name may be added but never replace raw.
Represent aliases as explicit observations/relations; do not treat alias similarity as cross-case identity.
Retain raw number and add normalized number separately.
Retain raw registration string and normalized representation separately.
Decompose addresses without discarding the original address string.
Preserve exact citation text and source location; canonicalization is a separate resolution operation.
Preserve source unit and numeric value; normalized unit is additional.
Preserve source precision; do not infer exact incident time from form metadata.

required_behavior: Generate candidate links before asserting SAME_AS.
Record the evidence/features contributing to a candidate match.
Maintain positive and negative resolution decisions.
Do not use a single shared name as sufficient evidence for cross-case identity.

graph_constraints: Every relationship must reference valid source and target entity IDs.
Every inferred relationship must have epistemic_state=INFERRED.
Every relationship sourced directly from a document should have at least one provenance observation.
Every legal citation must preserve raw_citation.
Every LegalCrosswalk must specify relationship_type and authority_source.
Unknown actors may be represented using stable unknown IDs and must not be silently resolved.
Event participants and targets must remain role-specific; do not collapse them into a generic connected_to edge.
A Case may reference many Documents; a Document may be an annexure of another Document.
A source assertion cannot be upgraded to ADJUDICATED solely by model inference.
Every assertion must reference at least one supporting observation unless its epistemic_state is OBSERVED and it is structural metadata.
Every inferred assertion must reference an Inference object.
Every identity confirmation must reference an IdentityCandidate with status=CONFIRMED and recorded supporting/contradicting evidence.
Every analytical result must preserve the input assertion/observation IDs that produced it.
Audit events are append-only and do not replace evidence provenance.
Raw source payloads and raw text are never overwritten by normalization.

schema_checks: No object without a stable ID.
No relationship without source and target IDs.
No legal citation without raw citation text.
No inferred relationship without inference status.
No normalized value without retaining raw value when source text exists.
No cross-case SAME_ENTITY_CONFIRMED link without recorded resolution evidence.
No inference result without model/algorithm version.
No identity confirmation without candidate-link evidence.
No analytical result without traceable input IDs.

implementation_order: 1. Validate the ontology JSON and supporting definitions with JSON Schema.
2. Register source, acquisition and source-record metadata before transformation.
3. Convert all source material into immutable Observation-first records.
4. Extract entities, attributes, events, relationships and legal citations with provenance.
5. Apply deterministic normalization while preserving raw source values.
6. Generate candidate identity links and record positive/negative resolution evidence separately.
7. Construct Assertions from validated observations; keep epistemic state explicit.
8. Project validated assertions into the typed graph with schema/domain constraints.
9. Run temporal, spatial, corroboration, contradiction and network analytics.
10. Represent model-derived results through explicit Inference objects.
11. Provide evidence-grounded Q&A and relationship explanations that resolve to source spans.
12. Enforce access policy, audit logging and retention controls in deployment.
13. Run extraction, relation, identity, provenance and unsupported-inference QA before release.

source_corpus_notes.reason_for_multi_case_design: The corpus provides variation needed to generalize the ontology across trafficking, narcotics, weapons, explosives, terrorist attacks, social-media activity, military/security attacks, financial observations, vehicles, casualties, and unknown actors.
source_corpus_notes.important_caveat: This ontology is a v0.1 prototype based on the supplied FIR corpus. It should be revised if later documents introduce materially new entities or semantics.
